walkthroughs.body_html: Pop Art began in 1950s Britain and exploded in 1960s America. Artists used mass culture — adverts, comics, packaging — as subject matter.
Andy Warhol screen-printed Marilyn Monroe and Campbell's soup cans. Roy Lichtenstein blew up comic panels using huge Ben Day dots to imitate cheap printing.
Pop Art questioned why a painting in a museum was 'higher' than a cereal box on a shelf. It made bright, bold, immediate work that anyone could enjoy.
